question: Determine the general solution of the differential equation $$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=\sin x,$$ on an interval where $\cos x\neq 0$, by identifying its standard linear form and applying the integrating factor method.
explanation:
Standard Form
The given equation is $$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=\sin x.$$ It is already in the standard form $$\frac{dy}{dx}+Py=Q,$$ with $P=\tan x$ and $Q=\sin x$.

Integrating Factor
The integrating factor is $$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int\tan x\,dx}.$$ Since $$\int\tan x\,dx=\log|\sec x|,$$ we may take $$\text{I.F.}=\sec x.$$ Multiplying the differential equation by $\sec x$, $$\sec x\frac{dy}{dx}+y\sec x\tan x=\tan x.$$ The left-hand side is the derivative of $y\sec x$, so $$\frac{d}{dx}(y\sec x)=\tan x.$$

Evaluation
Integrating, $$y\sec x=\int\tan x\,dx+C=\log|\sec x|+C.$$ Therefore, $$y=\cos x\left(\log|\sec x|+C\right).$$

Final Result
The general solution of the given linear differential equation is $$y=\cos x\left(\log|\sec x|+C\right),$$ on an interval where $\cos x\neq 0$.
